questions.q: Why does the profitability requirement use Gross Margin % rather than just Gross Margin in dollars?
options: Margin percent answers 'which categories drive margin' directly — a category can have high revenue and poor margin, and the VP specifically asked about margin
Percentages are always more accurate than dollar figures
DAX cannot calculate dollar-based margin at all
Gross Margin in dollars was never calculated in this model
questions.explain: Lesson 84's requirement was specifically about margin, not revenue — a percentage answers that question directly, since high revenue doesn't guarantee good margin.

questions.q: Why does the reseller fulfillment measure need USERELATIONSHIP()?
options: ShipDateKey's relationship to DimDate is inactive by default (OrderDateKey is active), so USERELATIONSHIP() activates it just for this calculation
USERELATIONSHIP() is required for every DAX measure regardless of relationships
ShipDateKey has no relationship to DimDate at all
USERELATIONSHIP() permanently changes which relationship is active for all future measures
questions.explain: This is the exact scenario Lesson 87 set up: only OrderDateKey's relationship is active by default, so calculating anything based on ShipDateKey requires temporarily activating that specific relationship.

questions.q: What DAX pattern does the year-over-year trend measure use, and why?
options: Variables first (VAR), then a single RETURN — the readability pattern Chapter 5 taught, instead of deeply nested parentheses
A single unnamed expression with no variables at all
It avoids using CALCULATE entirely
It requires a separate table just for prior-year data
questions.explain: Using VAR to name CurrentSales and PriorYearSales before a single RETURN statement is the variables-first pattern Chapter 5 emphasized for readability and debuggability.

questions.q: What DAX function compares a value to the same period one year earlier?
options: SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR
USERELATIONSHIP
DIVIDE
COUNTROWS
questions.explain: SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR is the time-intelligence function used inside CALCULATE to shift the filter context back exactly one year for comparison.

questions.q: What check does the lesson recommend before moving on from DAX measure-building?
options: Confirm every measure traces back to one of Lesson 84's four numbered requirements — remove or question anything that doesn't
Confirm every measure uses USERELATIONSHIP() at least once
Confirm there are at least twenty measures in the model
Confirm no measure uses the DIVIDE function
questions.explain: The discipline check is requirement traceability: a measure that doesn't map to one of the four written requirements from Lesson 84 is worth questioning before it's kept in the model.
